open_points.subject: A10 approval mismatch handling during run advancement
open_points.text: "when that one is approved and the send's digest differs, rule 1 applies and a new approval is requested"
open_points.question: When an existing approved approval no longer matches `request_digest`, must the kernel create the replacement `requested` approval in the same advancing request, or only after a later user request reaches the node again?
options: Create the new approval request immediately in the same advancement pass and keep the run `awaiting_approval`
Leave the run waiting without creating a new approval until a later advance request re-enters the node
open_points.default_guess: Create it immediately in the same advancement pass.

open_points.subject: A15 ordering of synthetic non-executed node records
open_points.text: "Records of nodes that become non-executable together are written in (`node_id`, `map_index`) order"
open_points.question: What exact procedure defines the set of nodes that "become non-executable together" (especially through transitive `upstream_failed` / `skipped_by_guard` propagation across mapped elements)?
options: Compute a full fixpoint set first, then write one sorted batch
Propagate iteratively and write records as each wave is discovered, sorted within each wave
open_points.default_guess: Compute the full set for that propagation step, then write one sorted batch.

open_points.subject: `stored_value_bytes_max` checks for `many` value ports
open_points.text: "each value ... is within `stored_value_bytes_max`; for a `many` port, is a JSON array whose every element fits it"
open_points.question: For `many` value inputs/case values, is the size ceiling applied to the whole serialized array value, to each element, or to both?
options: Ceiling applies to the whole array value only
Ceiling applies both per element and to the whole array
open_points.default_guess: Apply the ceiling to the whole array value (as one stored value).

open_points.subject: Trace completeness when a run ends by owner refusal/cancel
open_points.text: "Refusing writes one NodeExecution `refused_by_owner` for the refused element and ends the run `refused` ... nothing further is sent"
open_points.question: When a run ends `refused` or `cancelled`, should unconcluded downstream/independent nodes receive synthetic NodeExecution records (for example `upstream_failed`), or remain without node records?
options: Do not create any additional node records once run is terminal by owner decision
Emit synthetic terminal node records for still-unconcluded nodes
open_points.default_guess: Do not create additional node records after `refused`/`cancelled`.
